races.name: Zyn Pole Position EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Ancestor
runners_data.note: William Haggas's three-year-old has won and placed on Good going in both career starts (2/2 in similar conditions), making the surface no concern; Tom Marquand rides a horse with a clear front-running mandate and the licence to control fractions in a three-runner field, and the step up from 10f to 1m2f at Haydock looks straightforward given the pedigree and training profile.

runners_data.name: Golden Caviar
runners_data.note: Ed Dunlop's hold-up operator arrives just eight days after its last run and has posted back-to-back fifth-place finishes, including on Good ground at Sandown, which offers little encouragement about the finishing kick in this company; Hector Crouch will need a stronger pace than Ancestor is likely to set to deliver this horse from the rear, making the tactical situation awkward.

runners_data.name: Tropical Sands
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's lightly raced three-year-old carries a 57-day absence and switches from Soft and Standard surfaces to Good turf, with both previous runs over shorter trips — three unknowns stacking up simultaneously; Clifford Lee will likely track Ancestor in the absence of any other obvious lead companion, and the style is genuinely uncertain, but improvement to beat an OR=120 rival would need to be significant.

races.paceDynamic: Ancestor is the sole confirmed front-runner in this three-horse field and will lead from the outset at Haydock's 1m2f, facing zero pressure to dictate the fractions on Good ground. With Golden Caviar a hold-up type and Tropical Sands stylistically unknown, Ancestor controls every aspect of the tempo — able to set a measured, energy-conserving gallop that plays directly to stamina and front-running efficiency. The pace will almost certainly be steady to moderate, meaning there is no guaranteed strong finish to catch a well-positioned leader who has dictated throughout. This race shape emphatically favours the front-running profile: Ancestor gets a soft, uncontested lead and can pick the moment to extend, leaving hold-up horses like Golden Caviar dependent on a strong late pace that nobody is likely to generate.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ancestor Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Ancestor bowls along in front at a controlled tempo and is never headed, stamping its class on the race from flagfall.
scenarios.body: Ancestor dictates every fraction unchallenged, uses its good-going form (2/2 in similar conditions) and Haggas/Marquand combination to deliver a measured front-running display; with no rival capable of pressuring early, the horse simply wins on its own terms.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Flourish Bridges Gap
scenarios.trigger: If Ancestor sets an overly strong early gallop that leaves it exposed in the final two furlongs, inviting a late charge.
scenarios.body: An unexpectedly brisk early pace from Ancestor would drain its reserves, theoretically opening a window for Golden Caviar to close from off the pace; however, Golden Caviar's two fifth-place finishes in similar company provide slim confidence in the finishing kick materialising.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Unknown Quantity Surprises
scenarios.trigger: If Tropical Sands, lightly raced and stepping up from softer ground and shorter trips, proves significantly better than current form suggests.
scenarios.body: Ed Walker's lightly raced three-year-old is an unknown commodity on Good ground at this trip, and if the 57-day break has sharpened it, Clifford Lee could track Ancestor before challenging; the form and going profile are both unproven, making this a speculative scenario requiring genuine improvement.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Pace Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Tropical Sands or Golden Caviar adopts an unexpectedly aggressive role, creating a contested early tempo.
scenarios.body: Neither Golden Caviar nor Tropical Sands has shown any front-running inclination, so a contested early gallop requires both racing out of role simultaneously — an unlikely but not impossible disruption; even so, the disruption would be transient and Ancestor's class advantage likely prevails regardless.

watchPoints.text: Ancestor's early fractions are critical — if Tom Marquand sets an overly slow gallop, the race becomes a sprint finish that even Golden Caviar could contest from behind.
Golden Caviar's short turnaround (8 days) bears monitoring at the track; if the horse appears below par in the paddock or early in the race, its hold-up chance diminishes further.
Tropical Sands is 57 days off and lightly raced — watch for any market move or paddock signs of fitness, as the unknown style and going switch could produce a surprise either way.

With only three runners and one confirmed leader, any stumble or interference at the start involving Ancestor would radically alter the race shape and hand Golden Caviar a scenario it cannot otherwise engineer.

races.name: Zyn In The Moment Amateur Jockeys' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Dream Harder
runners_data.note: Won last time out 8 days ago over 1m2f on Good (similar going, 11 placed efforts from 15 relevant runs), handling step up to 1m6f is the key unknown, but trainer Mark Loughnane fires with 2 from 17 over 14 days and Jack Loughnane (7lb claimer) adds further weight allowance; natural hold-up horse who needs a contested pace to be seen to best advantage.
runners_data.comment: Dream Harder won last time out and returns fit on just eight days' rest, with experience over today's trip and going working in his favour. He carries 157 lb on a mark of 72, but his profile makes him the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Fast Fred
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer who finished second at 1m2f on Good last time out, and has a second over 1m6f on the card (Tapeta); Pippa Brown's 3lb claim helps at the weights and the horse's front-foot style maps neatly to tracking Clansman — the 27-day break is not a concern given recent fitness.
runners_data.comment: Fast Fred ran a fine second last time out and has experience of today's distance and going, making him a genuine danger; the concern is that he has found only one winner in his last six starts, suggesting consistency could let him down.

runners_data.name: Caph Star
runners_data.note: Prominent runner whose recent form is almost entirely at shorter trips (ten furlongs), and this 1m6f test represents a clear stamina stretch — trainer Mark Rimell fires at 1 from 5 over 14 days and Harry Rimell's 7lb claim softens the OR=74 burden; the tongue-tie is retained and Good ground suits based on a 1W4P record in similar conditions.
runners_data.comment: Caph Star arrives in fine fettle on 15 days' rest, and his recent string of placed efforts — third two starts back and runner-up last time out — marks him as a consistent threat; the chief concern is whether he can convert that place form into a win carrying 155 lb.

runners_data.name: Clansman
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner with two all-weather wins at 1m6f (Southwell Tapeta) giving him strong trip experience, though he has not run on turf Good ground recently; 41 days off could have him fresh and his ability to control tempo unchallenged makes him structurally dangerous regardless of raw ratings.
runners_data.comment: Returned a winner two starts back but unplaced last time out, and 41 days on the sidelines adds a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and going, and his speed rating offers mild encouragement, though 152 lb is a stern burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Made All
runners_data.note: Holds a solid placed record (0W5P) at 1m6f-2m1f on Good ground and rarely beats rivals home — five thirds in the last five Good-ground runs illustrates consistency without a winning punch; Rebecca Hitchen's 5lb claim helps and the tongue-tie is positive headgear, but the pattern of placing without winning is a clear flag.
runners_data.comment: Made All has shown consistency with back-to-back thirds in his most recent starts, but a winner five starts back and unplaced efforts in between suggest he's a tricky conveyance; going experience helps, though his 151 lb burden is a significant ask at a rating of 70.

runners_data.name: Arrange
runners_data.note: Strong recent form at exactly 1m6f on Good ground (2nd twice in last five), making him one of the most course-and-distance-qualified horses in the field; a natural hold-up horse whose best racing comes from off the pace, and with the field holding more rear-of-field types than the race shape can accommodate, he may not always get an unimpeded run — his 7-day turnaround is tight but the trainer's recent 0-from-5 record dampens confidence.
runners_data.comment: Arrange has been knocking persistently on the door, finishing second in each of her last two starts, and she has experience of today's trip and conditions — the main concern is whether she can finally convert, having been winless in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Edward Sexton
runners_data.note: Last five runs came over 7f-1m on Tapeta/Polytrack, so this 1m6f turf assignment represents a dramatic step into unknown territory both in trip and surface; Gary & Josh Moore send him out after a 109-day absence, and while the 2-from-19 trainer form over 14 days is modest, the horse's natural hold-up style would need genuine pace to work from — his profile carries the most unknowns in this field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, all finishing sixth or seventh, Edward Sexton has been consistently below par and returns after a 109-day break carrying 146 lb — with our figures ranking him seventh of eight, it is hard to make a case for him here.

runners_data.name: Havachoc
runners_data.note: Progressive four-year-old with a string of placed efforts (0W1P on Good, stronger on Tapeta) and a prominent racing style that suits tracking the pace; at OR=58 he carries the lightest weight in the field and Lucas Murphy's 5lb claim compounds that advantage, though Good turf at 1m6f is a surface-and-trip combination where his form is thin.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with a fourth last time out following a string of minor positions, Havachoc is hard to fancy ranked bottom of the field on our figures; he has run over today's trip and going before, but offers little encouragement at the weights.

races.paceDynamic: Clansman is the sole confirmed front-runner and, unopposed for the lead, will set a controlled, honest gallop over this 1m6f trip on Good turf — there is no pressure horse to force him into an unsustainable tempo, so expect him to dictate from the front at a pace that suits his own stamina profile. Fast Fred, Caph Star, and Havachoc will press forward into prominent positions behind him, creating a compact early order rather than a strung-out field. Arrange and Edward Sexton are genuine hold-up horses who cannot both find their natural berth at the rear given the number of prominent types ahead of them — of the two, Arrange's recent 1m6f Good-ground form (twice second at this trip and going) gives him the better claim to the position that suits him, while Edward Sexton, stepping up sharply in trip from shorter-distance all-weather races, is the more compromised. A lone front-runner setting a measured pace over a stamina trip on Good ground classically favours strong-staying prominent types who can track and pounce in the home straight, with pure hold-up horses carrying extra tactical risk given the moderate tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Clansman Controls, Prominents Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Clansman leads at a sustainable gallop and one of the close-tracking prominent horses outlasts him in the straight.
scenarios.body: Clansman's uncontested lead creates a well-strung, rhythm-favour scenario where Fast Fred or Caph Star, both proven prominent racers on Good ground, can sit a length or two off the pace and drive past in the final furlong; at 1m6f on Good going, the horse with the superior finishing stamina rather than raw speed wins.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Clansman Front-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so conservative that Clansman steals an unassailable lead and the field fails to close.
scenarios.body: An amateur-jockey field may misjudge the tempo, allowing Clansman to dictate margins unchallenged into the straight; his 1m6f course form (two wins at this trip on Tapeta, with recent Flat winners) makes him dangerous if the field sleeps.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and a deep closer can weave through in the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: Dream Harder, who landed a recent win and has course form at 1m2f on Good, is the most naturally suited closer in the field and would benefit if the early tempo lifts; Made All has strong placed form at this trip on Good but her name belies a hold-up tendency in practice, and she is consistent without quite winning.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Pace, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the amateur jockeys produce uneven pace fractions that disrupt the expected race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: A bunched finish becomes possible if tempo surges mid-race then stalls, handing Arrange — who has legitimate place form at 1m6f on Good ground twice — a chance to emerge from an unexpectedly crowded closing straight; Edward Sexton, raw over this trip, is a long outsider in any shape but could sneak a frame.

watchPoints.text: Clansman — if he clears 2+ lengths at halfway with no jockey in the field applying pressure, the race could be over before the straight; watch for amateur riders failing to recognise the danger early.

Arrange — a genuine 1m6f Good-ground performer (2nd twice) whose true hold-up style may be compromised by traffic if he cannot find clear daylight in the straight; watch his position rounding the final turn.
Caph Star — all five recent runs have been at ten furlongs or shorter, so watch early in the straight for signs he is being stretched by the extra half-mile before the whip comes out.

Dream Harder — came into this race on an 8-day turnaround after winning; watch for whether the jockey positions more prominently than expected given the step up in trip, which would signal the team believes stamina is not a concern.

Edward Sexton — 109-day absence and a sharp step up in trip from all-weather sprinting; watch the first half-mile to see whether he travels with the field or drops away immediately, as either outcome will clarify his chance rapidly.

races.name: Zyn Pacesetter Cup Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: God Given Talent
runners_data.note: William Haggas in strong form (10 from 52 over 14 days) and Tom Marquand is a powerful booking; won on good ground over 6f most recently and drops back to 5f which may sharpen responses, with a 21-day freshen-up the only mild query on a horse that has strong prominent-tracking credentials on similar going.
runners_data.comment: God Given Talent won three starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, with 21 days between runs leaving him fresh enough to deliver; the concern is that his last two outings have both disappointed.

runners_data.name: Dance A Jig
runners_data.note: Back-to-back placed efforts at 5f on good and soft ground show this trip suits; Ralph Beckett's yard at 6/50 is moderate and a 51-day absence is the key concern, but natural prominent style means the horse should slot just off the pace and get a fair run in this straightforward race shape.
runners_data.comment: Twice runner-up in recent starts, Dance A Jig lines up as the top-rated runner here and brings solid placed form to today's trip; yet to land a win from his last three, the 51-day absence is the one query, though connections saddle him with 135 lb from stall four.

runners_data.name: Jaijai
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's consistent sprint performer has won and placed repeatedly on good ground over 5f, is the only confirmed leader in the field, and quick 7-day turnaround suggests connections are confident; the danger is whether a solo front-runner over 5f can sustain enough pace to repel the pack without overdoing it early.
runners_data.comment: Jaijai brings solid recent form — a winner three starts back and second two starts back — and has experience of today's trip and conditions, carrying 131 lb from stall 3; the unplaced effort last time out is the one note of caution.

runners_data.name: Undercover Affair
runners_data.note: Solid nursery profile with a win and multiple placed efforts at 5f on good — this horse's real preference is to race prominently, but with Jaijai plus two other prominent types ahead of it, the race map places it in midfield and the 0.93 STYLE_FIT flag tempers its overall chance accordingly; Ryan Kavanagh's 3lb claim is a minor positive.
runners_data.comment: Undercover Affair won two starts back and was third three starts back, with two wins in his last six starts, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions carrying 129 lb; the main risk is an eighth last time out suggesting he needs to bounce back.

runners_data.name: Rotelle
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes-trained two-year-old who bolted up over 5f good on debut but only has two runs to assess; a natural up-with-the-pace type who will find prominent ground harder to secure in this race shape, and the redistribution to midfield means its finishing effort depends on breaking cleanly and working through horses — Paddy Bradley needs to ride enterprisingly.
runners_data.comment: Rotelle won two starts back but was beaten well last time out, and he ranks last on our figures here; he has run over today's trip and going, and draw one is noted, but it's hard to fancy at these weights against stronger company.

runners_data.name: Casino Star
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's consistent juvenile has two runner-up efforts on good ground at 5f and 6f, but being a prominent horse pushed furthest back in the race mapping means it faces the steepest ask; Clifford Lee must hope for a fast pace to chase down from behind, and the 0.80 STYLE_FIT flag reflects how far outside its natural role this scenario places the horse.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts despite a couple of placed efforts, Casino Star has run over today's trip and going before and steps in from stall two carrying 124 lb — modest profile on our figures, though those seconds suggest he's rarely far away.

races.paceDynamic: Jaijai is the sole confirmed front-runner and, at 5f on good ground at Haydock, will stride directly into the lead from the gates with Sean Levey likely to control tempo from the outset — recent form of 1-2-1-2 on this surface shows this horse thrives in this role. God Given Talent and Dance A Jig are natural prominent types who will press for the early lead positions just off Jaijai, creating a compact, sustainably-paced contest rather than a truly hot gallop. This field holds more prominent types than can all get their preferred positions: Undercover Affair and Rotelle are genuine up-with-the-pace horses who will be crowded out and forced to race further back than ideal, compromising their chances in any shape that depends on them running from midfield. With one unchallenged front-runner setting a manageable tempo over this sprint trip, the shape strongly favours horses that can travel prominently and sustain their effort through to the line — a truly lead-dominated or clean prominent-tracking profile is the chief beneficiary.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jaijai Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Jaijai secures the lead uncontested and sets an honest but not suicidal tempo, dictating throughout on ground that suits.
scenarios.body: Jaijai has won twice on good going over 5f and clearly relishes front-running, and a field lacking genuine challengers for the lead means Levey can balance the pace perfectly; prominent trackers will finish strongly but may not get there.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul
scenarios.trigger: If God Given Talent or Dance A Jig travel better than Jaijai and hit the rising ground with a decisive turn of foot.
scenarios.body: God Given Talent's Haggas/Marquand combination carries significant trainer-in-form clout and a 21-day freshener suits; Dance A Jig ran two consecutive seconds over 5f on this surface and creeps into the picture if Jaijai has gone slightly too fast early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Crowded-Out Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Undercover Affair or Rotelle recover from their compromised positions more quickly than expected and arrive late with sustained momentum.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires both horses to race well outside their natural comfort zone — Undercover Affair's STYLE_FIT of 0.93 and Rotelle's 0.90 reflect genuine positional compromise, making this outcome structurally less likely; if the pace collapses in the final furlong it becomes possible but remains the minority case.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rear Emerges Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and Casino Star, shuffled back furthest of all, finds a clear late run to mow down a tiring field.
scenarios.body: Casino Star has form figures of 2-6-2 and clearly needs a strong gallop to produce finishing effort, but as the horse most out of role in this race shape — a natural prominent type mapped to hold-up — the conditions required are the least likely to materialise.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether God Given Talent tracks Jaijai aggressively from the off — if Marquand sends it up to press the leader through the early stages, Jaijai's front-running advantage is instantly tested.
Monitor Undercover Affair's draw and early jump — if it breaks sharply it may force its way into the prominent group despite the race mapping, changing the competitive dynamics significantly.

Rotelle's starting price and market move are worth tracking given it is lightly raced (two runs only) and Charlie Fellowes will have a clearer read on its readiness than the form book currently shows.
With the going confirmed Good across all distances at Haydock today, there is no ground-related wildcard — pace and positional luck will be the decisive factors rather than any surface variance.

Jaijai's 7-day turnaround bears watching in running: if the horse shows any sign of tiring earlier than expected on the turn for home, the two trailing prominent types (Undercover Affair, Rotelle) become live factors even from their compromised positions.

races.name: Zyn Frontrunner Finish EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
Zyn Strong Stride EBF Fillies' Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Find Your Zyn Moment Stride Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Distinct Spirit
runners_data.note: Six-year-old who has won twice from his last four starts over a mile on Good, handled by Kubler yard in sharp form (4/12); dropping back to 7f is a mild question given all recent wins have been over 8f, but he travels prominently and can secure a genuine chasing position here.
runners_data.comment: Distinct Spirit arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and has run over today's trip and going, making him a potent threat at 140 lb; the short six-day turnaround is the one question mark his connections must answer.

runners_data.name: Farandaway
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner, Grant Tuer's four-year-old has won twice over 6f on fast ground but limited Good-going experience (6/15 sim-going); the step to 7f is within compass given recent form, and an uncontested lead flatters their chance considerably more than raw ratings suggest.
runners_data.comment: Farandaway arrives in fine nick — a winner two starts back and placed last time out, returning after just 15 days — and has experience over today's trip and going. The main risk is whether 135 lb blunts his finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Montezin
runners_data.note: Antony Brittain runner wearing tongue-strap, rated 73 but recent form is uninspiring with a best finish of fourth in similar company; five of his last five runs show no win or placed finish and he has not excelled on Good at this trip — hard to frame a winning case.
runners_data.comment: Montezin shaped with promise when fourth three starts back and returns here just 13 days later with experience over today's trip and going; winless in his last five starts, but our ratings just about favour him and he looks the one to beat from stall 2 off 134 lb.

runners_data.name: Criminal Shore
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's hold-up specialist wears a visor and won over 8f on Tapeta last time; his Good-ground form is limited (0W1P in similar conditions) and he typically needs a strongly run race to close from the back — gets that chance if the pace is honest enough.
runners_data.comment: Criminal Shore won three starts back but has since posted an unplaced effort and a sixth, and his speed rating of 69 leaves him vulnerable against stronger rivals; he has run over today's distance and going before, though stall ten and 134 lb are notable asks.

runners_data.name: Raffles Angel
runners_data.note: Jack Jones's five-year-old is a consistent prominent racer who has finished third in each of her last two starts over 6f on Good; stepping up to 7f on a flat track looks a fair test, and her record of 4W8P on similar going suggests she handles conditions well, though the trainer has drawn a blank in nine runners over 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Twice third in her last two starts, Raffles Angel arrives here in decent nick after just 15 days, has experience over today's trip and conditions, yet remains winless in her last five — her consistency keeps her in the mix, though breaking through looks the challenge.

runners_data.name: Potomac River
runners_data.note: T J Kent's hold-up four-year-old has run three times at 7f on Good, placing twice; his trainer is in sharp form (3/4 over 14 days) and Jack Mitchell is an astute judge of pace — needs the race to develop steadily to get into it from the back.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a sixth last time out, Potomac River has hit a flat patch in form and ranks ninth of eleven on our figures; he has run over today's trip and going before, but little in his recent profile makes him easy to recommend from stall 11 off 132 lb.

runners_data.name: Evocative Spark
runners_data.note: John David Riches' seven-year-old is a genuine front-runner by nature — three wins and three places at 7f on Good in recent starts — but with the field packed with prominent types, he is unlikely to get anywhere near his preferred early position; visor in place, 69 days off, and racing out of role tempers enthusiasm significantly.
runners_data.comment: Evocative Spark has winning form in his recent starts — a winner two starts back and two further wins in his last six — yet a seventh three starts back and a fourth last time out temper expectations, and 69 days off the track is a fitness query at 132 lb.

runners_data.name: Tokyo Joe
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's four-year-old is naturally suited to racing up with the pace over 6-7f, and Tom Marquand takes over in the saddle; the trainer is in excellent 14-day form (11/40), but with Tokyo Joe pushed into midfield by the congestion of prominent types, his chance is considerably diluted compared to races where he can race handily.
runners_data.comment: Tokyo Joe arrives on the back of a win last time out, and his trainer is in cracking form at 26% over the past fortnight — he's a serious threat here; the main concern is whether 131 lb from stall seven blunts his finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Invincible Ruby
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's four-year-old has won three times over 6f on Good and finished second in this exact trip-and-going combination; in isolation a strong profile, but the reality of this field means he will race from further back than he has done in those winning efforts — the style mismatch is the key dampener.
runners_data.comment: Invincible Ruby ran second last time out and has a win two starts back, showing consistent recent form, though she carries a stiff 129 lb from stall 9 and ranks seventh of eleven on ratings — in-form but up against it on weight.

runners_data.name: Magic Music
runners_data.note: Steph Hollinshead's four-year-old won over 7f on Good and has placed three times at the trip; 42 days off is notable and the trainer has had no winners from seven runners over the past fortnight — a horse who wants to be prominent but will find himself racing through traffic instead.
runners_data.comment: Magic Music has not recaptured her winning form since a victory two starts back, finishing sixth last time out, and ranked tenth of eleven on our figures she faces a stiff ask here — though she has run over today's trip and going before and stall one gets her away cleanly.

runners_data.name: Bajan Bandit
runners_data.note: Patrick Morris's six-year-old wears a visor and has no wins or places in 15 comparable going runs, with all recent history over 8f on Tapeta or Good; Ryan Kavanagh claims 3lb but this is the weakest profile in the field by some margin, and like the other displaced prominent types he will not get the early berth he needs.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked last of 11 on our figures, Bajan Bandit does at least return after 31 days and has run over today's trip and going before — but a run of three consecutive sixth-place finishes and a fifth two starts back make him hard to fancy here.

races.paceDynamic: Farandaway is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 7f Haydock handicap and, with no genuine rival likely to press them hard from the gates, they should be able to control tempo at a sustainable rather than scorching gallop on Good turf. Behind them, Distinct Spirit and Raffles Angel are natural prominent types likely to occupy the chasing berths, while Evocative Spark, Tokyo Joe, Invincible Ruby, Magic Music and Bajan Bandit are all true prominent racers who cannot all claim their preferred position and will be shuffled into a compressed midfield — none of them operating in their natural role. Criminal Shore and Potomac River are the genuine hold-up horses in the field, likely to race from the back of a tightly grouped pack. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all get their position; Distinct Spirit and Raffles Angel, as the highest-rated and most experienced prominent types, are best placed to actually secure those chasing slots alongside Farandaway. A controlled, single-pace gallop on Good ground at Haydock 7f heavily favours hold-up horses or genuine prominent racers who can settle close to a steady pace and quicken late — runners who can travel smoothly and produce a finishing effort into the straight are the primary beneficiaries, while the displaced prominent types forced to race out of role face a significant tactical disadvantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Farandaway Controls, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Farandaway sets a sustainable, uncontested gallop and the pace proves just honest enough to set up a finish for those tracking smoothly.
scenarios.body: Farandaway leads without pressure through the first five furlongs, establishing a steady rhythm that allows the genuine hold-up horses and settled prominent types to travel comfortably before unleashing their effort in the final two furlongs; this steady-pace scenario on Good Haydock turf typically draws out the best in horses who can quicken off a sound gallop rather than those who have had to battle for position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Override
scenarios.trigger: If Distinct Spirit or Raffles Angel tracks Farandaway closely from the outset and kicks before the displaced midfielders can respond.
scenarios.body: One or both of the natural prominent types sits a length or two off Farandaway's lead, producing their effort from a position of comfort while the compressed midfield pack is left with too much ground to make up in the short Haydock straight; at a fair pace this shape rewards horses who have raced handy all their lives rather than those forced into an unnatural position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Pair Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Farandaway quickens dramatically in the straight and the field fragments, leaving those who tracked the lead to dominate.
scenarios.body: Should the pace increase sharply from the front two furlongs out, the field strings out and horses racing in the chasing positions — already on the bridle — inherit the race as the hold-up horses cannot close the gap in time on a flat track; this benefits those who have successfully tracked a fast-finishing leader in their recent form history.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Displaced Prominent Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is unexpectedly brisk and Farandaway is outpaced or tires, releasing one of the compressed prominent types into the clear.
scenarios.body: A scenario that requires multiple things to go wrong simultaneously — Farandaway tiring, the race developing unusually fast and one of the redistributed horses (Evocative Spark or Tokyo Joe, both winners at this trip) finding clear daylight from mid-division; this is the least likely shape because it depends on horses performing optimally while racing out of their natural role.

watchPoints.text: Farandaway's ability to control tempo unchallenged is the single biggest tactical factor — if Distinct Spirit's rider Ebrahim Nader pushes forward early to test their lead, the whole pace map shifts and the resulting battle could collapse both horses' chances in the final furlong.

Evocative Spark, Tokyo Joe and Invincible Ruby are all true prominent horses likely to jostle for position in the first two furlongs — watch for early crowding and potential interference as five or six horses attempt to occupy three or four natural positions.

Criminal Shore and Potomac River both need a truly run race to close from hold-up — if Farandaway sets only a dawdle, neither can generate enough momentum off a slow pace over 7f on flat Haydock turf, effectively removing them from contention before the straight.

Magic Music is 42 days off a run and Steph Hollinshead's stable has had no recent winners; any market support for this horse into the race should be noted as a potential market mover, but the layoff combined with the unfavourable race shape warrants caution.
